summary_html: Case results in **child fatality or serious injury**, triggering mandatory federal and state review. Data and lessons inform systemic reform.
authority_html:
- **Protect Our Kids Act (PL 112-275)** — establishes national commission and reporting requirements  
- **CAPTA §5106a(b)(2)(A)(x)** — mandates public disclosure and case review of fatalities

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Willis S. Sheldon, Individually and as Administrator of the Estate of Dezirae Sheldon v. Nicholas Ruggiero
key_cases.holding: Summary judgment for a DCF administrative reviewer was affirmed because the mandated-reporter duty under 33 V.S.A. § 4913(a) is triggered only by reasonable cause to believe a child has been abused, and a repetitious allegation adding nothing new did not supply it.
key_cases.relevance: This is the Vermont child-fatality case defining the limits of individual liability after a death of a child known to DCF.
key_cases.quote: In this context, as a matter of law, defendant did not have reasonable cause to make a report.

key_cases.holding: SRS (now DCF) owed the reporting children an actionable duty of care because 33 V.S.A. § 4915 imposes mandatory investigative acts for the protection of a particular class, and sovereign immunity did not bar the negligence suit.
key_cases.relevance: Sabia is Vermont's leading authority permitting damages actions where agency inaction allowed continuing serious harm to a child.
key_cases.quote: Accordingly, we conclude that SRS had a duty to protect plaintiffs under the circumstances of this case.

key_cases.case_name: LaShay v. Department of Social & Rehabilitation Services
key_cases.holding: A caseworker supervisor was not entitled to official immunity on a claim that he ignored warnings about a foster home where the child was later sexually abused, and SRS waived sovereign immunity to the extent of its liability insurance.
key_cases.relevance: It permits a damages action for serious harm suffered by a child while in state foster care.
key_cases.quote: Further, if reporting were mandatory, it was a ministerial, not a discretionary duty.

key_cases.case_name: Estate of Sumner v. Department of Social & Rehabilitation Services
key_cases.holding: Summary judgment for the Department was affirmed because no reasonable jury could find that its alleged negligence in supervising and placing a CHINS youth proximately caused that youth's rape and murder of his seven-year-old cousin; the youth's independent criminal act was an intervening cause the Department had no duty to anticipate.
key_cases.relevance: Sumner is the counterweight to Sabia at this node: a child died in circumstances traceable to a placement the agency knew had collapsed, yet no liability followed because the fatal act was not foreseeable to the agency.
key_cases.quote: In this case, a reasonable jury could not have concluded that the Department had a duty to anticipate Steven's rape and murder of Crystal Sumner.

key_cases.case_name: Tina Stocker v. State of Vermont
key_cases.holding: Judgment as a matter of law for the State was affirmed: the only non-discretionary DCF duty supporting a damages action is the 33 V.S.A. § 4915 duty to record a report and make an initial determination whether it is valid, assessment and investigation under §§ 4915a and 4915b are discretionary and within sovereign immunity, and plaintiffs could not show the recording failures proximately caused the children's continued abuse.
key_cases.relevance: It is the current Vermont ceiling on damages actions for serious harm to children known to DCF and should be read with Sabia and Sumner as the third point of the special-duty line.
key_cases.quote: any implied right of action against DCF based in this statutory scheme is limited to violations of mandatory duties pursuant to § 4915
